name: composite-gallery
title: Viva-munk Composite Gallery
lead:
viva-munk models populations of growing, dividing cells with 2D physics (pymunk) and shared
chemical fields, built on process-bigraph. This investigation gathers one study per composite
so each mechanism can be run, visualized, and inspected on its own. Every study has a real
completed simulation; its animation is rendered post-hoc from the emitter results, exactly as
in the published demo report.

at_a_glance.role: Show surface colonization: cells settle, adhere, and begin secreting EPS.
Demonstrate pressure-inhibited growth in multi-segment (bendable) cells.
Show emergent colony / biofilm architecture from many interacting cells.
Reproduce run/tumble chemotaxis up an exponential attractant gradient.
Track lineages in an open chamber where cells crossing the right wall are removed.
Couple cell growth to a shared, diffusing nutrient field and show local depletion.
Show protein-aggregate (inclusion-body) burden and asymmetric segregation at division.
Reproduce single-channel trapping: one cell per dead-end channel, progeny pushed into the flow channel.
Show density-dependent autoinducer signaling: cells switch ON above a local threshold.

how_to_read:
Start with the simulation GIF in each study (or the gallery report at
/reports/composite-gallery.html) to see the behaviour, then read the study card and biological
summary. attachment / biofilm show colony formation; bending-pressure / inclusion-bodies show
mechanics and aging; chemotaxis shows motility; glucose-growth / quorum-sensing show field
coupling; mother- and daughter-machine show device geometries.

glossary.definition: A wired set of processes (physics, growth, fields, signaling) run together as one model.
The compositional simulation framework viva-munk is built on.
The 2D rigid-body physics engine used for cell mechanics and contacts.
Extracellular polymeric substance — the secreted matrix of a biofilm.
Saturating growth-rate law μ·S/(Km+S) used for nutrient-limited growth.
A diffusible signal whose concentration encodes population density (quorum sensing).
An intracellular protein aggregate that burdens growth and segregates asymmetrically.

biological_story:
Bacteria live as physically interacting populations in structured, chemically heterogeneous
environments. viva-munk assembles that picture from composable parts: capsule-shaped cells with
realistic 2D mechanics that grow, divide, push on each other, and bend; diffusing concentration
fields they consume or secrete into; and behavioural rules layered on top — chemotactic
run/tumble, quorum-sensing feedback, inclusion-body aging, and surface attachment. Each study in
this gallery isolates one of these mechanisms so it can be seen clearly, while sharing the same
underlying cell, physics, and field machinery.
question:
Can every viva-munk composite from the published report be reproduced as an individual,
runnable study in the dashboard, with its simulation GIF shown on the report?
hypothesis:
Each composite, run with the demo defaults, qualitatively reproduces its published panel —
surface attachment, pressure-limited bending growth, biofilm packing, chemotactic gradient
climbing, mother/daughter device kinetics, nutrient-coupled growth, inclusion-body aging,
and density-dependent quorum sensing.

executive.what_is_this:
A gallery of the nine viva-munk multi-cell composites, each run as its own study with a
simulation animation and a short biological write-up.
executive.verdict: All nine run and qualitatively reproduce the published demo; re-verified reproducible on the current stack; not yet quantitatively calibrated.
executive.reproducibility:
Re-verified 2026-09-23: all nine composites re-ran end-to-end (baseline + reference
variant, 18 runs) on the current framework — vivarium-workbench 0.3.87,
process-bigraph 1.8.3, bigraph-schema 1.6.0, viva-emitters 0.2.3, viva-superpowers 0.22.0 —
at git dc92ed3, generation gen-20260924T021544Z-79a161. No run errored.
decisions_needed: Which composites need parameter calibration against literature before quantitative claims?
Which readouts should become pass/fail behavior tests?

scientific_argument.main_claim:
The viva-munk process-bigraph composites reproduce a broad range of multi-cell phenomena
(mechanics, motility, nutrient coupling, aging, signaling) in a single composable framework.
evidence_for: All nine simulations complete and produce the expected qualitative dynamics (see each study's GIF).
Re-ran end-to-end on the current stack (workbench 0.3.87 / process-bigraph 1.8.3 / bigraph-schema 1.6.0) at git dc92ed3 — 18/18 runs succeeded (generation gen-20260924T021544Z-79a161).
Mechanisms span physics (bending/pressure), motility (chemotaxis), fields (glucose, autoinducer), and aging (inclusion bodies).
evidence_against: Parameters use demo defaults; no quantitative fit to experimental data yet.
Readouts are declared but not yet enforced as pass/fail behavior tests.
caveats: GIFs are qualitative; calibration and behavior tests are future work.

Reproducing the re-run on the current stack needs a bigraph-schema JSON-encoder fix: process `_inputs` schema (String/Node Atoms) leak into gather_emitter_results and BigraphJSONEncoder cannot serialize its own Atom types. Handled here via a local encoder patch; an upstream fix is pending.
